title: A Sample-Free Compilation Framework for Efficient Dynamic Tensor Computation
problem: Dynamic-shape tensor computation requires shape-specific compilation; existing compilers rely on shape sampling, causing high tuning cost and poor performance on unseen shapes
motivation: ML workloads increasingly have dynamic shapes; shape sampling is expensive and inefficient; sample-free compilation could enable better generalization
method: Helix compiles tensor code (numerical arrays) without requiring specific shape information beforehand by decomposing the compilation task across the computer's architectural layers—from high-level programming abstractions down to low-level machine operations. It uses a bidirectional strategy: applying optimization rules top-down while building concrete machine kernels (instruction sequences) bottom-up. At lower architectural levels it measures performance directly, and at higher levels it estimates performance to avoid expensive measurement.
key_novelty: Helix eliminates the expensive shape-sampling step in dynamic tensor compilation by organizing the compiler around the computer's architectural hierarchy instead.
contributions: 174x compilation time reduction; 2.26x-3.29x speedup vs existing compilers
limitations: Evaluation limited to selected tensor operations; scalability to very complex dynamic shapes unclear
primary_theme: Sample-free compilation for dynamic tensor workloads
